title: Do p-optimal propositional proof systems exist?
formal: Is there a Cook–Reckhow propositional proof system that polynomial-time simulates every other Cook–Reckhow proof system?
context:
Simulation must translate proofs in polynomial time, with the polynomial allowed to depend on the simulated system. Ordinary optimality is also mentioned in the source and is related to the existing optimal-proof-system record; polynomial boundedness is a different notion.

This question was found through Wikipedia and compared individually with the existing candidate and archived records. The linked literature provides definitions and background; this import is not a completed research-card review.
why: Asks whether one efficiently checkable proof formalism can efficiently absorb every other such formalism.
